lines.english: "Touma."
"Touma… hey… sorry to bother you, but I need you to wake up for a bit."
"…Hmm?"
"Ahh!? Excuse me, sorry… you're Touma Kazusa, right?"
"You haven't attended school since the opening ceremony, right? Have you been sick?"
"…Huh?"
"I do realize that we weren't doing much in classes while you were absent, but there were a lot of notices and forms handed out…"
"Here are the textbooks for all your subjects, your student ID card, and all the forms in the order in which you should be turning them in."
"Oh, also… in case you need it, I got you a form to get the student ticket discount. You come to school by train from Iwazu-chou, right?"
"And this is the one thing you mustn't forgetーthe parent-teacher meeting printout. It's starting next week, so be sure to pass this on to your guardian."
"Guardian…"
"I was planning on bringing all this directly to your house, but I had a lot of things to do… Sorry about that."
"Do you have any questions regarding anything up to now? I'll try to answer what I can."
"…*shakes her head*"
"I see, that's good. Then…"
"Haah…"
"…Next, I'll explain how to fill out these documents. We'll start with the form for buying the school jersey."
"…What's the matter?"
"…noying…"
"Hmm?"
"You're annoying."
"I get that a lot, but this is important. If I'm annoying you, then do your best to memorize it all the first time so I don't have to repeat it."
"Ah… that's right. We haven't met before. I'm Kitahara Haruki. For what it's worth, I'm the class representative for Class E for the first half of the year."
"I didn't ask for your name."
"Well, your face had 'Who the hell are you?' written all over it, you see."
"…Hold on, are you still feeling sick after all? Do you want to go to the nurse's office? I can take you there."
"…Don't touch me."
"Hm? No, I haven't actually touched you yet."
"…I understand. We can do this later. Oh, that's right! If you'd like, I could take these to your house after school…"
"Don't touch me!"
At the time, I'm pretty sure I retorted in my mind with, "Pretty sure I haven't touched you at all."
But to begin with, she… the way Touma Kazusa kept using the phrase, "Don't touch me" wasn't in its literal sense.
I must have realized soon enough that it was akin to a "keep out" warning… that she was telling me not to get involved with her all along.
"Hey, are you listening, Kitahara?"
I was so consumed by boredom… or rather by self-admonition, so much that I'd unconsciously escaped to the past.
Well, the memories I escaped to weren't really all that beautiful either.
"Tell me, why'd you do something like that? You know full well how badly hurt you could have gotten if you'd fallen from there, right?"
"Ah, umm, that was… I'm sorry, I wasn't thinking straight at all."
"Well, even if you insist that's the case…"
It's been a day since that mess.
Despite the fact that I was scolded right on the spot, it'd become so much of a problem that the homeroom teacher also lectured me the next morning.

"This isn't like you, Kitahara. Normally you'd be the one preventing others from acting out like this. Did you think that since you're not the class representative anymore that you can just toss out your responsibilities?"
"No, that's not what I… I'm sorry."
"I bet Touma was the one who provoked him anyway. There's no way Kitahara would do something so ridiculous all on his own."
"W-What? Umm, I'm not sure I understand what you mean. Why are you making it sound like it's Touma's fault now?"
In fact, I don't even understand why Touma was dragged in here to be scolded as well.
"I thought that'd be the end of it when you left the music program on your own, but you're still nothing but trouble even among the regulars. Touma, do you even plan on graduating?"
The music program…? And she left on her own…?
"Besides, I was against letting Touma use Music Room 2 exclusively."
"Wha…?"
"Her parent may be a famous pianist, and said parent might have made a sizable donation to the school, but all that special treatment's starting to get to her head."
"I-Is that so?"
"Suwa-sensei, that's enough… I'll be sure to reprimand Touma myself."
For some reason, the conversation is moving away from my misdemeanor.
With all these unexpected and unreasonable accusations being thrown around all over the place, I don't even know when to cut in anymore…
"…Hey, why are you reprimanding Touma? And why is she being blamed alongside me? I'll have you know, she saved my life."
Since I can't stop the conversation from going off-topic, all I can do is bring up that cheap sense of justice of mine for now.
"Ugh…"
"Ah, well, you know…"
"Haa…"
…As expected, of all their reactions, hers was the coldest.
"I've warned you many times, Kitahara. A serious, hardworking guy like you shouldn't get involved with Touma. You don't want to waste your university recommendation, do you?"
"I'm the one you should be angry with. This has nothing to do with Touma, does it?"
"Is she really not involved? Are you sure Touma isn't just getting you to say that?"
"Haaahhh… Say something, Touma…"
"Touma…"
"Aah, jeez… I'm so tired…"
I used up all my energy before classes even started… I'm confident I'll be sleeping through first period.
Still though, the attitude those teachers had… What was that? Just thinking about it makes me sick.
Ahh, I know it's not my problem but… No, the fact that it has turned into her problem is the issue here.
"Unbelievable… Why do I have to put up with this…?"
"You should have said that earlier, not now!"
It's too late to regret it now.
"It's pointless to tell the teachers anything. Adults won't understand a thing."
"What's up with that hackneyed rebellious attitude? You're sounding like a delinquent from the Showa Period…"
"Shut up!"
"Ah…"
"…What is it?"
I have so many things I want to ask her, but…
"…It must have been terrible for you. I'm sorry, it's all my fault."
"I'm 100% sure that your idiocy is to blame for this, Kitahara."
Judging by her expression, I get the feeling Touma isn't all too opposed to the idea of just forgetting about what happened.

"Still, you know, I guess that's the result of my everyday general attitude. If you gained the trust of the teachers, Touma, they might end up needlessly covering for you like they did for me, you know?"
"I refuse to live a calm, boring life like yours… all while sucking up to those above me."
"My life goal, you see, is to live longer than average people."
"You really are a dull guy. The stereotypical class representative, no doubt about it."
"Well, I was the class rep for the first term…"
"You know, I've been wanting to tell you this for a while now…"
"Ah…"
Touma's thin, white finger points straight at me to condemn my words…
And then, seeing someone running down the hallway toward us, she unnaturally brings her finger down.
"Kitahara-kun!"
"Ogiso…? Why?"
"I heard it all from Iizuka-kun… Are you okay? Your fingers aren't hurt or anything, right?"
"Well, I'm not hurt… W-Whoa!"
"Hmm… I can't tell just by looking at them. Your fingers weren't injured, right? You almost fell from the window, didn't you?"
She nonchalantly lifts up my hands, then spreads them out and carefully investigates them in worry.
I'm glad that she's worried about my injury, but the way Ogiso's fingers are caressing the palm of my hand right now is… it's, how do I say this, quite, um…
"I'm fine, I'm fine, I'm fine already! I'm not hurt anywhere. Anyway, that's not what you should be worried about!"

I instinctively raise my hands above my head so Ogiso can't reach them, relinquishing myself of the blissful sensation of her hands. With that, any chance of explaining myself in a cool-headed manner is out the window.
"Ah, okay… Well, what was the punishment?"
She crosses the fingers she used to embrace my hands earlier over her chest, staring at me with a cute gesture.
"Yeah… They said they'd decide later. Well, I don't think it'll be anything like a suspension, disciplinary action, or suspension of club activities."
"I see… That's a relief. There's only a month left until the school festival, right?"
…And I guess her occasional glance to her right is also a form of affectionate gesturing?
"Yeah, you're right… What a relief…"
"Hm? Kitahara-kun?"
True enough, it doesn't seem like any severe punishment will be levied on me.
However…
"Yeah… What a relief. Since you went through the trouble of joining us, Ogiso, it'd be terrible if we couldn't perform at the school festival."
"Revocation of the Light Music Club's privilege to use the music room."
The very possibility of such a "light punishment" as suggested by Suwa at the end would have been fatal to us right now.
"You're right, it would be really frustrating if we couldn't perform over some silly accident, now that I've finally decided to join."
"I'm sorry for being silly…"
"Ah…! Umm, that's not what I meant! I wasn't trying to blame you or…"
"Well, anyway, sorry for making you worry. For now, let's leave it at that."
"Alright. Yup, I was really worried. So be sure to reflect deeply on this."
"S-Sorry!"
"Just kidding, a few minutes should be enough, hehe!"
"O…Ogiso…"
"…See you."
"A friend of yours?"
Back then, I hadn't noticed it at all.
How perfect Ogiso's timing had been… How Touma's expression had changed ever so slightly…
"Ah, that's right, Ogiso, let me introduce you to her."
"Hold on… I'm not…"
"She's Touma Kazusa. …She's our keyboardi…
Oww!?"
"Don't screw around, you idiot!"
"A…Ahaha…?"
After half a year of knowing her, I'm happy that I can casually put my hand on her shoulder, and have her casually punch me with clenched fists in response.
She's no longer saying, "Don't touch me" to me.
"Can't keep up at all…"
"…Guess she's still angry."
So this is Touma when she's not holding back.
Hearing her play unrestrained by my clumsy guitar does sound incredibly cool, but… personally, it just makes me sad.
"Touma Kazusa. Class 3-E, number 32 on the class roster. Part of the go-home club. Address is 6-2-12, Iwazu-chou. Telephone number…"
"You can find all that in the class registry."
Actually, I've memorized the whole thing. Just one of the duties of a class representative.
That's normal, right…?
"But you don't know this, do you? Her class last year was 2-H. The year before that, it was 1-H…"
"She may be our classmate, but that doesn't mean you should go prying into her past."
"You were perfectly content digging through all her other personal info, though."
Class H…
The last class for each year. In other words, the music program's class.
"Well, in that case, it's no wonder I'd never seen her until last year."
Classes A through G are in the main building. A new building was added for the music program three years ago. Class H stays there, so they never interact with us.
"That wasn't the only reason, it seems…"
"What do you mean?"
"She'd been absent for almost half of second year, and barely passed."
"Could it be, she had problems with her health last year?"
"According to rumors, and from my own experience, the problem appears to have been her personality."
"She still has a bad personality even now, but she's properly coming to school. Although she is late most of the time."
"That's your idea of a defense?"
"…Wait a sec. Something you just said bothers me. What do you mean, 'From my own experience'?"
"The first time I saw her was in your classroom, and three days later I tried to ask her out, but she just kicked me out of nowhere!"
"Wait, wait, wait! What were you thinking, acting without a single word of permission from me!?"
I feel beyond exasperated.
"Well… she's the prettiest girl in your class by far, isn't she? She's the only one I'd ask out, you see."
"You won't be satisfied until you have a girl from every class? Do you plan to get 24 girlfriends across all years and classes?"
His immoral line of thought… no, rather, his sharp sense and ability to identify the very finest leaves me in awe…
"No way, I'd definitely pass on the music students. So that makes 21 in total…"
"You don't deserve the company of other guys."
All the girls he's been trying to introduce me to were without a doubt from that 21…
"It's a thing of the past, let's just forget about it. Besides, it's not like she's your girlfriend or anything, right?"
"T-That's… true, but…"
Why am I… at a loss…?
"Umm, y-you know, uh, Takeya…"
Why am I… stuttering…?
"…Even if she isn't, somehow you're getting along with her."
"W-Well, on the surface, her personality seems bad, but deep inside… I mean, if you get to know her, she's not a bad friend… besides, she sits next to me."
"While we're on the topic… it seems that up until last year, she'd never even talked with any of the other music students."
"Touma Kazusa, you see… was a model student ever since she enrolled in the music program."
From this point on, Takeya starts giving me some incredibly detailed info on her, so detailed and accurate, in fact, that I can't help but believe him.
The only problem is that most of the information he knows is centered around her gender.
During first year, she participated and won in the national competition.
Matsukawa finally placed third at the same contest this year, but she'd already dominated in it two years ago. Touma was in a different league from the very beginning.
At first, the music teachers had all praised Touma. When compared to Touma, her classmates all appeared to be inexperienced amateurs.
Even so, if only she had acted like a normal model student, her classmates would've respected her without fear and would've aspired to be like her without avoiding her.
"Touma Youko…?"
However…
It would seem that there's something else that, even now, continues to antagonize the relationships she has with others…
"Would that happen to be…?"
"Yeah, in other words…"
"She's Touma's mother, right? I think I remember seeing her name in the guardian register…"
"I figured you'd say that, but it creeps me out that you remember that much."
"…Well, what about her mother?"
The truth is, I only know the name of several specific parents. Luckily, he does not pursue the matter further.
"Do you remember, Haruki… there was a whiskey commercial or something years ago, with a lady in a red dress playing the piano."
"Umm… Was that during elementary school? I think they had a series of commercials, with one top artist appearing for each one…."
"Yeah, yeah, that! Anyway, the pianist was the first one in that series."
"Aaah, yeah, there was something like that! I'm sure my mother bought the CD, even though she isn't a fan of classical music at all."
"Yeah, so, in other words…"
"…Ah… You're kidding."
No, I remember…
It's true that I remember seeing it credited to Touma Youko on screen. I'm about 80% certain of it.
"She was performing in Japan at the time, it seems she's in Europe now."
"Touma's…?"
Despite being a classical pianist being a small occupation in Japan, her CDs were very popular.
On top of that, it's selling incredibly well, even in the countries where classical music was born.
"Apparently, she donated a substantial amount to our school. The piano in Music Room 2 comes from the Toumas as well."
Her mother happens to be an extremely famous celebrity, even on her own turf.
And if she's also made such a large donation to the school, no wonder the staff would give Touma special treatment..
Yes, for example… preferential treatment, like one music room out of the three being put aside specifically for her use.

"Touma Kazusa had been the gold standard of a student since the music program was established… The teachers were partial to her, and she had status, money, and fame. She was most certainly a student who was given the highest graces…"
"With all of that put together, everyone in her class hated her, and Touma showed no signs of wanting to meet them halfway either."
In other words…
She was snarling at both the teachers and her classmates equally for looking at her through tinted glasses.
"By second year, she was barely talking to any of her classmates."
"What's with that… What was the class representative doing!?"
"Normal class representatives don't act like you, being so irritatingly nosy, mediating between people, and dealing with every single thing."
"…They don't?"
Isn't it the representative's job to grit their teeth while taking all the jobs others wouldn't want to do?
…Even if it means that other people may end up hating them.
"Well, with all that, she really couldn't stay there much longer. And then she transferred to the regular program, which brings us to now."
"I see…"
"Well, what'll you do? Will you still try to recruit her into the club?"
With so many emotions swirling around in my mind, I can't immediately provide him with an ideal, logical response like I always would.
"She's going to be a difficult one, that girl. She might refuse, despite getting along with you."
All I can say is that I feel frustrated, and it feels like my rationality is being overshadowed by my emotions. And I'm terrible when it comes to emotional reasoning.
"After all, she even brushed someone like me off. For any other man to be capable of opening up her heart would be…"
"Shut up, you one-girl-per-classist."
Even so…
"I'll recruit her."
"Haruki…"
Because her piano once matched up with me…
"I'll do whatever it takes to make her one of us."
Because I was enchanted by that sound…
"She's that good, isn't in any clubs, and is in the regular program… There's no reason not to invite her, right?"
On top of that, it's because… she's the one who played that beautiful melody…
"How do you plan on telling Ogiso? You're still lying to her about the pianist, right?"
"I'll explain it properly to her. And I'll apologize too. But… I'll make sure she understands that we absolutely need Touma."
"And if she doesn't agree?"
"I won't give up. Because I absolutely need the two of them. They're both invaluable."
"That's what they call two-timing…"
"I never thought I'd be hearing that from you."
I may very well be doing something despicable right now.
I'd be lying to someone who'd joined me because they trusted me, and I'd be causing a lot of trouble for a friend who'd saved me.
But I can't stop now. I don't want to stop either.
There's only one month left until the school festival.
There isn't any time left to think this over, have any regrets, or lose my way now.
"Well, anyway, there's just one thing I should warn you about."
"Hey, that's usually my line…"
"I don't mind you recruiting Touma, but don't do it out of some odd sympathy for her. She'll only be offended if you go out of your way for her."
"I know that."
"Also, don't go off lecturing like you always do. I know you mean well, but there are also times when you should really take a step back."
"No need to tell me twice. I understand myself the best."
"Someone like her would no doubt find your pushy, stubborn attitude annoying. Be really careful, okay?"
"I'm telling you… I won't do annoying things like that. I've been getting along with her for half a year, you know? There's nothing to worry about."
"I'd like to believe that, sure…"
"Having you sitting there is annoying."
"Don't use that word all of a sudden."
The next day, after hearing about Touma's experience these past two years from Takeya…
Right after school, Touma headed straight for Music Room 2, and just as she opened the door…
"What about your practice? You've only got a month left."
"I was thinking of avoiding that music room until they decide on my punishment."
She found a certain annoying former class representative sitting there, fully prepared to play the part of her eager audience.
"Do you honestly believe you'll make it acting so carefree like this?"
"It'll be fine. In a few days, we'll get someone amazing to join us."
"Well, congratulations…"
"I see, so you're glad about that too. Then let's get straight to…"
"Though, if I was in this amazing person's shoes, I wouldn't get on your pathetic excuse for a boat, even if I was stranded in the middle of the Pacific Ocean."
"…You sure have become talkative, Touma."
Compared to what I've heard from her since the beginning of spring this year… her vocabulary has since expanded beyond expressions like, "Shut up", "Get lost", or "Don't touch me"…
"Even if I remain silent, a certain idiot who can't take a hint will just keep talking anyway."
"…Could I just stay and listen?"
"You're bothering me, so get lost."
"Mm…"
"Though, even if I tell you that, I have a feeling you won't leave."
"You sure know me well. As expected of a friend."
Personally, I think it's nice that she now follows up with expressions other than, "Shut up", "Get lost", or "Don't touch me."
…Though I would like it even better if we could just start a conversation without having to go through all that trouble.
"Haah…"
Is she aware that I'm looking her way…?
Regardless of whether she is, I can only sigh in admiration of Touma's finger movements.
I mean, I can't even keep up with how fast she's moving.
Not only do her fingers move along the keys at incredible speed, but they also easily move from one side of the keyboard to the other. Something that should be hard for her slender hands to do.
Being the amateur I am, I can hear nothing off-key. I can't clearly hear every note, but I can't tell her apart from a professional… Well, I guess that's what makes me an amateur.
"Ah…"
It's possible that Touma can no longer feel my presence here.
After all…
The look on her face right now is one she normally wouldn't show anyone.
Without me realizing it, she started making use of that "privilege of ignoring me," which she'd earned a month after we met.
"Touma!"
"Touma… Hey… Come on, wake up!"
"…Hmm?"
"Good morning. Rare to see you arrive before class starts."
"…Haa…"
"You don't have to look so obviously annoyed."
"Good morning! Good morning, Touma! The bell will ring soon, so please, wake up already!"
"Mmm… Mmmph…"
"Look, I'm sorry for waking you up, but the career interest survey is due at lunch today."
"…Huh…"
"I'll be collecting them for the teacher. I figured you probably threw out the form, so here's a new one. I already filled in what I know, like your name."
"I won't look at what you write. It'll go straight in the envelope, and I won't take a peek whatsoever. So, well, um, please fill it out before lunch."
"No, don't just roll it up. Fill it in properly."
"I'm not interested in this."
"If you want, you can just write 'university,' 'find employment,' or just 'I haven't decided yet.' The teacher said that you should at least write your current thoughts, or lack thereof."
"Besides, if you're so interested in bothering me, why don't you go collect everyone else's forms…?"
"I picked everyone else's forms up yesterday. Yours is the last one."
"…There were about three people absent yesterday, weren't there?"
"I gave them a phone call and picked the forms up at their houses. They filled them out, even though they were sick."
"…Stupid?"
"That's a cruel thing to say. Our classmates are all serious, you know."
"Who do you think I'm talking about…?"
"Besides, the school is affiliated with a university, so you can write down, 'Enrolling in Houjou University.' They couldn't care less if you just wrote that down."
"There's just no way I'm going there."
"So you don't want to lie…? You're more sincere than I thought. I'm impressed."
"…Don't jump to your own conclusions and see me in a better light. It's annoying."
"If you don't want people to reevaluate their opinion of you, just going along with the flow would work out better, you know."
"What are you saying?"
"Look, that way people wouldn't be so impressed when you give a rare display of good conduct and evaluate you more normally, right?"
"I have no intention of letting anyone evaluate me."
"I don't recommend filling out the form during class. If you can, try to get it done before the first bell…"
"You really are…"
"Well, this decision could have an effect on the rest of your life, so you can think about it for a little longer. I'll leave it up to you, then."
"Ah… Good, good!"
"…Kitahara…"
"Is there something you're not sure how to fill out?"
"I'll do as you ask, so you can at least listen to one of my requests."
"Ahh, of course! If there's anything bothering you, I'm sure I can help…"
"If I ignore you from now on, don't worry about it. I'm just extremely annoyed and disgusted."
"I… I see."
"Here, I'm done. Take it."
"Whoa, don't throw it at me. You should turn it over first…"
"I don't really care if you look at it. I just wrote, 'Enrolling in Houjou University,' like you said."
"…Are you going to?"
"Who knows?"
"…I see."
"Are we done here? I'm going back to sleep, then."
"Ah, sorry. One last thing."
"…What?"
"I get it… From now on, I won't mind if you ignore me or anything."
"Ah… Okay."
"So please don't hold it against me if I keep on rambling anyway, Touma."
"…Huh?"
"Good morning, Touma. Great weather we're having today, huh?"
"Just wait a second, Kitahara. That's not how the promise…"
"I'll do as you ask, so isn't it only fair that you listen to one of my requests?"
"This isn't 'just one thing'! How shameless can you be!?"
"Touma… don't tell me you've just noticed that now."
Since that day…
Touma was willing to allow me to say things like "good morning" or "goodbye."
…Though, of course, she never really replied.
"Like I said, I understand everything now. I know all about how you've spent the past two years."
"I think it's unacceptable that you'd be excluded from your class over stuff like your mother being famous or the teachers favoring you."
"Still, you know… although this may sound quite painful, I think you should try to get along with everyone."
"How should I say this, conveying your feelings doesn't only include the positive stuff. Negative feelings like hate or unwillingness are also part of it."
"You might hate smiling at first. But even if you force yourself to smile, your smile will reach those around you. And if others smile back, then you'll also come to enjoy it."
"I think living that way is a lot better in comparison. No, I guess I'm not sure if people our age would understand such a line of thought."
"Ah, so, this introduction was a bit long, but what I wanted to talk about was…"
"…Out."
"Hmm?"
"…Get out."
"Touma?"
"Get out. Don't come here ever again."
"Wait, I was about to get to…"
"Get ooooout!!!"
"Uwaah!?"
Afterward…
Even if I called from the other side of the door, Touma wouldn't unlock the door to the second room again.
Why…?
What did I do to make her so mad? I wasn't doing anything out of the ordinary…
"…Anyway, I'm sorry. I lied to you a little, Ogiso."
"Hmm…"
Ogiso looks at the sky through her fake glasses, as if she has no interest in what I just said.
"That pianist from before wasn't actually a member of the club… she just happened to be in the classroom next to us, and played with us from time to time."
"But you guys were in such perfect sync. I heard it from the rooftop every now and then, it seemed as if you guys were having so much fun…"
"That's only because she matched her pace to mine… No matter how badly I messed up, she would help the song take shape…"
"Hmmm…"
Ogiso still doesn't show any interest, toying with her braids.
"Umm… Are you angry?"
"At?"
"Well, you know… at me for lying that we had a keyboardist. There really isn't anyone else other than you and us guitarists."
"That was just me getting the wrong idea. There's no reason for you to apologize, Kitahara-kun."
"…Really?"
"Is there something else still bothering you?"
"No… I guess that's fine, then."
"If it's fine, then it's fine, right?"
"Y…Yeah…"
Even though she says that, what's this strange oppressive feeling I'm getting?
During the short time I've known Ogiso, I have never seen her angry, but…
If something like that were to really happen, I'm quite sure that this is exactly how she'd act… Or is it just my imagination that I feel this way when looking at her right now?
"Ah, and, well… sorry about your job."
"Kitahara-kun, you've been doing nothing but apologizing for a while now."
"Still, I should be apologizing for what happened. I mean, I was the one who forcibly dragged you into this."
As it turns out, today was Ogiso's last day on her job.
"It's fine, I never felt pressured to do this."
"Really?"
Going with the excuse that she was focused on the school festival, she left her part-time job that was perfect for a student like her.
"I did enjoy this job, you know? I got to meet so many people, learn so many things… and most of all, I earned a decent amount of pocket money, too."
Even so, I waited at the exit as Ogiso was held up by the manager and part-time lady. They were all talking, weeping, and giving farewell gifts.
…It seems that even at her part-time job, her usual personality was well-liked.
"But in the coming month, I'll get to experience a completely different form of joy, so I don't regret it, you know?"
"Eh? Yeah…"
"I'm looking forward to it, Kitahara-kun."
"Y-Y-Yeah… right. Umm, yeah… we've gotta do our best."
Before I knew it, Ogiso's expression had changed into a genuine smile, one different from earlier.
Her expression is, well… Let's just say she looks deviously cunning, such that it's more than enough to soften up whoever's looking at her, even through those fake glasses.
However…

Unable to bear the awkwardness any longer, Touma was just about to say, "I'm leaving" when this young man appeared like a savior, bringing tea..
"Which means you're taking entrance exams. Are you going to be enrolling at our school?"
"Grades-wise, I could make it, but it might be impossible financially. Dad's all burned out just from enrolling her there."

In total, the lot is about 200 square meters large, and the house takes up about half of it. Its first floor has a living room, a study, and a master bedroom, while the second floor has the children's rooms; a stereotypical "detached home."

"On top of that, if she continues her studies in Houjou University… I don't know if we'd be able to afford my entrance tuition."
"I-I see… Well, hang in there."

"…What?"
"You're nervous, aren't you?"
"Ah, Takahiro-kun, don't be scared. She's just really shy, you see."
"Ah, well… I am scared, but only a little bit."
"W-W-Wha…"
"Loosen up a little, would you? He's acting more maturely than you are."
"W-We…Well I, look… who could have predicted this turn of events…?"
"Still though, I think this is the first time my sister has brought friends home since she enrolled in Houjou."
"Ah, really now…"
I suppose it's due to her misunderstood reputation of being the school's number one lady.
"She had plenty of friends come over during middle school. She'd throw her birthday parties inviting all the girls from her class… Twenty of them in this tiny house, can you imagine?"
"…That's what I thought, yeah."
Despite being so sociable and ordinary, Ogiso had to start worrying about maintaining her image due to that trivial rumor.
Whether she's an ordinary girl or an unattainable flower, it doesn't change the fact that Ogiso is overflowing with charm.
"And now she's bringing friends home again, six months before graduation. I wonder what brought about this change."
"Well, about that… there's something that the three of us absolutely have to discuss today."

"Ah…"
"She doesn't seem to understand our feelings at all… No matter how many times we tried, she wouldn't accept."
"Umm, so basically, you mean… you're trying to untangle this complicated relationship between the three of you?"
"No, umm…"
"Ah, I guess you could put it that way. Touma here's pretty stubborn, as you can see."
"Wait a second, Kitahara…"
"What, am I wrong? Feel free to voice any objections you have."
Yeah, we won't settle for a compromise today.
We're down to the wire, where the slightest thing will tick off Touma, and either she'll become our ally, or she'll never talk to us again.
"That's not what I mean… He'll definitely get the wrong idea from what you just said…"
"Huh? What do you mea…"
"Sorry to keep you waiting! Wha… Takahiro? What are you doing here?"
"Oh, crap."
"Crap?"
Ogiso frowns a bit as she looks at the three of us in the room, carrying a large, steamy tray.
"I told you not to bother us, didn't I? Your sister and her friends have something really important to talk about. Come on, get out! Right now!"
"O-Oh…"
"Sister…"
She sternly raises her eyebrows, looking like a typical sister scolding her younger brother. I've never seen something like this before.
"Ah, well, umm… Your guests seemed a bit neglected, and I had some time to kill, and you left them here without even bringing them tea, and…"
"I'm sorry, Nee-chan."
"Ohhhh…"
"Uwaah…"

"Hmm… Maybe I went too far. Dinner is ready downstairs, so go eat. I was the one who made it today, so I can't really guarantee the taste."
"Mm… Thank you."
"They made up so fast-!"
What is this…? It feels like I've seen something I shouldn't have.
"Ah, and Nee-chan…"
"Hm? What is it, Takahiro?"
"I'm not sure when you got yourself into this mess, but…"
"Eh?"
"U-Umm, well, uh… Good luck. I hope you manage to settle everything peacefully."
"…What's he talking about?"
"Who knows?"
"Ignorance is bliss sometimes…"
"Sorry, things were a bit of a mess down there. That's why preparing this took a bit longer than expected."
"That's fine, or rather… Ogiso, this is…"
"Let's eat first. The heat will at least help mask the flavor."
Yellowtail teriyaki, chop suey, and Hamburger steak. The main dishes are a magnificent blend of Japanese, Chinese, and Western cuisine.
On top of that, rice and shijimi soup too. No matter the dish, she took into consideration how the colors and appearance would match up when plating them. A perfect example of a "family dinner."
With how great it looks, it's guaranteed that the flavor will at least be average.
"Why…?"
"Because Kitahara-kun said that he wanted to talk over dinner."
"Well, I did say that, but…"
I'd meant some place quieter where we could talk, like at a family restaurant or a cafe.
"It's cheaper to be eating dinner at home. And besides…"
"Besides?"
"It's bad for Touma-san's health if she always eats out, so I thought I might kill two birds with one stone."
"H-Hey…"
I thought I warned her many times that Touma is particularly hot-tempered…
"Well then, Touma-san, help yourself. You won't be able to fight on an empty stomach."
"T-Touma…?"
Should I say Ogiso is fearless, or that Touma is just defenseless against her…?
"Well then, let's eat.
…Kitahara-kun?"
"Y-Yeah, let's eat.."
"Touma-san?"
"Ohh…"
"You can have as much as you'd like. There's enough for seconds too, so don't be afraid to ask."
I really can't understand the dynamic between these two.
"Here, Kitahara-kun. Please have some."
"Y-Yeah… Thanks."
For some reason, we were completely silent for the entire duration of the dinner.
I'm not sure what Touma was so stubborn about. Since she was so focused on eating up everything she grabbed, there was not much we could really discuss…
"Here, Touma-san."
And once Touma had eaten it all, Ogiso asked her with a smile if she wanted seconds.
After several seconds of tension, Touma silently handed her rice bowl to the smiling Ogiso.
And this, perhaps heart-warming scene, repeated itself at least twice.
During this time, I had only managed to ask for seconds once.
"Well, how did you guys like dinner? I think it turned out okay, but…"
"Ah, yeah… It was delicious."
"Really? I'm so glad! I only make food about once a month, so I didn't really feel all that confident, you see…"
"…Sip."

"…Sip."
I don't mean anything bad when I say it was by the book either.
It's because she followed the instructions in the book carefully that she was able to make something like this in practice. She'll only get better from now on.
"…Sip."
Given that she's already produced such results with only normal effort, I have no doubt that I can expect greater things from her from here on out.
"Whew…"
"Would you like another cup?"
"Ahh, no, there's no need, thank you."
"What about you, Touma-san?"
"No need."
"I see…"
"Then, I'll be going home…"
"We absolutely can't let you!"
Though Touma tried to stand up, it's obvious that her movements have been dulled since she took on Ogiso's challenge and ate three whole bowls of rice.
"Come on Touma, can't you join us? We only have this little request that you help us with all sorts of things for the school festival."
"How can you call it 'a little request' and then ask for me to help with 'all sorts of things'?"
"I think that people who complain about every little detail will end up losing the trust of others."
"What a coincidence. I happen to agree with you, Kitahara."
For some reason, Touma is looking at me as if objecting to something.
"Come on, Touma-san, can't you help us with this?"
"…You can keep trying to appeal to my emotions like that, but I won't budge."
"Hm? What do you mean 'like that'?"
"Whatever you may try, be it sincerity, devotion, or goodwill… I'm not someone so weak-willed to fall prey to something so cheap."
"After all… I've never been a considerate person at all to begin with."
"Touma-san…?"
"Because of that, I'm sorry, but…"
"Kitahara-kun, I'm sorry, but… I'm not sure I understand what Touma-san is saying. Could you explain it to me?"
"Wha…?"

"Basically, Touma's saying that she sees your hospitality as some form of sincerity, devotion, or goodwill."
"Ahh, if that's what it is, then we can split the cost. Umm, I think it would be something like 1000 yen per person…"
"It's not about the money…!"
I get the reason why Touma can't deal with Ogiso, as well as the reason why Ogiso seems completely oblivious of that fact.
"So you see, Touma, Ogiso doesn't really think of today as anything particularly special."
"Why…? Bringing others to your house, having them taste your cooking… what for?"
"Maybe… you don't understand because your personalities are so different?"
Unlike Touma, Ogiso was simply raised that way.
…Although I'm sure she'd make even less of an effort to understand if I told her that, so I kept those words to myself.
In other words, their relationship was predestined to be turbulent because of this.
"Listen, Touma-san. I didn't treat you to all this because I had an ulterior motive. I just felt that we could talk more easily on a full stomach…"
Isn't that what it means to have an ulterior motive?
"…Do you expect me to believe that you have pure intentions, when you've already put me through so much torment?"
…I feel a bit ashamed for anticipating that very retort.
"Torment…? I was just teasing you a little!"
"Wrongly jumping to conclusions about other people's feelings, and embarrassing them until their face burns with shame. You call that 'just teasing'!?"
"Come on, Touma… what in the world did Ogiso do to you?"
"Ahh… that's probably because, Kitahara-kun, Touma-san is in…"
"Fine then, we'll leave the emotional arguments out of this! Let's be rational!"
Seeing this exchange between them makes it even harder for me to ignore factors other than "how they were raised"…
"For starters, the plan you guys have is just impossible…"
"Wait!"
"Ogiso?"
The moment Touma's words were about to flare up…
Ogiso puts out the flames with cold water, even though she was the one waiting for this topic to be brought up.
"I'm sorry, but… be quiet for a moment…"
Commanding us, she moves as if sliding across the floor, and as she reaches the door, she puts her hand on the knob.
"Hey, Takahiro. This doesn't seem as bad as you claimed it was."
"That's just for now. I'm telling you, it's going to get real ugly."
"Their relationship doesn't seem that bad to me. Sure, that girl didn't talk too much, but both of them seemed quite polite."
"I'm sure of it. I heard it from them. The reason why she came to our house is to make those two break up."
"Why would they talk about it here? And what does it have to do with Setsuna?"
"That's exactly why it's gonna get ugly. Basically, the reason why the two of them are fighting is…"
"C-Could it be that…?"
"That's right… Nee-chan stole her boyfriend, and things are about to go ballistic."
"That's… quite a mess. And how does that boy feel about this?"

"There wasn't the slightest hint that she was dating anyone… Yet now suddenly she's having an immoral affair… You're good, Nee-chan!"
"There's nothing 'good' about it at all! Betraying her friend in such a cruel way… I don't recall raising such an immoral daughter."
"Could you do something about it, Mom? As an adult, maybe something before they get into a scuffle…"
"I'm the one who wants to do something about you two!"
"Uwaah!?"
"I was wondering what those whispers I was hearing were… Takahiro! Just what kind of a person do you take your sister for!?"
"W-Well… see, I was worried about you, Nee-chan…"
"And Mom, it's always the same with you! You're still believing Takahiro's gibberish nonsense!"
"W-Well, you know… recently young people have been getting into those… what did they call them? You know, those friends-with-benefits relationships or something…"
"Jeez, Mom! Daytime dramas, variety shows and weekly women's magazines are all off-limits from now on!"
"A-Aha… Ahahahaha…"
"I-I'm so sorry! I never meant for you to bear witness to this side of my family. I humbly apologize for my mom and brother's rudeness!"
"T-That's okay, we don't mind… right, Touma?"
"…I don't care."
"I'm really sorry, Touma-san! My family is a bit overprotective, or rather, they're not really thoughtful…"
"W-Well… you guys get along and that's what's important, right?"
It didn't take much to convince Setsuna's family that we were part of the light music club, here to discuss our plans for the school festival.
…Though I'm not sure why they accepted it so easily. In any case, we're in a rush to resolve all our issues now, so I'll just leave it at that.
"We don't. We're always fighting."
"Really?"
"…Well, since they let me have a part-time job, I can't really go up against them."
"…I guess not."
Though she calls it not wanting to go up against them, it's probably more that she can't stay angry at them.
When Takahiro-kun and Setsuna's mother learned about our activities, they had a sudden change of heart. Satisfied, they said they'd definitely come to the festival.
Besides, Ogiso didn't tell them not to come or that she wouldn't like them to. In a way, she'd forgiven her family much sooner than we did.
"Were you offended? They really didn't mean anything bad. I'll apologize in their stead, okay?"
"I said I'm not angry. You aren't either, right, Touma?"
"Not really, I don't care."
How should I put it, this anticlimax has… left both Touma and me dumbfounded at how ridiculously well this family gets along.
"That's how it is, so we'll leave it at that. By the way, is it okay if we eat the cake your mother brought?"
"Ah, sure. Mom actually baked this one herself. She always bakes a cake at noon on her days off…"
Also, although I do feel sorry for Touma…
I definitely don't think of this as an unpleasant situation. In fact, it's the exact opposite.
It's that kind of embarrassing, nostalgic feeling you get from seeing a ten year old home video…
It makes me feel truly happy, if just a little.
"To begin with, the plan you guys have is just impossible to pull off. You're not going to make it in time for the festival, no matter who joins you."
"It won't be that way if you join us, Touma…"
I gulp down my cake and sip my black tea.
I also make sure no one is eavesdropping from the hallway.
It's almost 7 PM, and our negotiations have finally begun.
"In that case, Kitahara… what exactly would you have me do?"
"Well, the piano, obviously… In terms of band composition, you'd be the keyboardist, I guess. Anyway, I just want you to perform with us, Touma."
"We're… well, Kitahara-kun in particular is a huge fan of your piano, Touma-san."
"Please don't say that about me right in front of her…"
"At least deny it before getting embarrassed. You disgust me."
"Sorry…"

"And who will be the bassist? And what about the drums? Sure, it depends on the songs you pick, but you know that just adding a pianist won't be enough, right?"
"We can think of solutions to those problems as we go…"
"Even though you have only three weeks left? How many days will this 'as we go' take? All of tomorrow?"
"Well, if only you'd joined us sooner, Touma."
"O-One week, I think."

"There's no time for that. With merely two weeks of practice, what kind of results do you expect to achieve? If you perform like that, we'll just end up a complete and utter joke."
"Get it? This whole ideal plan you're talking about is already nothing more than a dream."
"Is… Is it wrong for me to dream…?"
"Kitahara-kun…"
I know it is, but still…
"It sure is."
"Instantly shot down!?"

"This isn't like you. I could never imagine such words coming out of the ever-realistic Kitahara's mouth."
"Do you think… I'm that rigid?"
"Preparing in advance, avoiding risks, keeping things stable. That's what defines you, isn't it?"

"…You sure seem to know a lot, Touma-san."
"We're not talking about me right now. Don't try to break my train of thought."
"Well, excuse me then… for acting so out of character."

"I didn't say it's something to be sorry about. I just said it's strange."
"But… what's wrong with a single month's leeway? A single month for me to act out of character, and embarrass myself."
"You might regret it. You might lose the whole 'serious, hardworking, honors student, class representative Kitahara Haruki' image you've had until now."

"…That puts you in utter contrast with my two and a half years."
"Sorry to tell you, but that goes without saying. I did my best to get on the teachers' good side, while you did your worst to get on their bad side."
"Ki-Kitahara-kun…?"
"So don't think you have me all figured out. Even I can be pretty unpredictable every once in a while."
"And I'm saying that's not like you…"
"For once, I don't care if you start hating me for it, but I'll still make sure you join us whether you like it or not! …If possible."
"…Wait a second, now. I've never said a word about hating you…"
"Eh?"
"Setsuna. I need to speak with you. Please open up."
And then…

"W-Wait, stop! Why are you bringing that up in front of my friends…?"
"That'd be because you lied, wouldn't it? You never told me anything about singing at the school festival."

"You should consult your father and mother before doing something like that. We promised to do that long ago, didn't we?"

"I'm sorry, but please have them go home. We have something very important to discuss as a family."
"You can't be…"

"Eh? Ah, Dad…!"
"Let's head home, then…"
"…Yeah."
"Whew…"

"Kept you waiting, huh?"
"You sure did."
"That's fine. I don't really feel sorry about it."
"Oh, really."
Touma was five minutes behind me. Finally leaving the entryway of the Ogiso household, she now stands beside me.
I start walking, and she shows no sign of hostility, disgust, or embarrassment as she walks beside me.
But I'm… a little embarrassed.
"By the way…"
"Y-Yeah?"

I really am… a little embarrassed.
"Ogiso apologized. She was half-crying."
"I don't mind at all."
"That's what I told her too."
"…Thank you."
"But that's just me telling her. You'll have to tell her that yourself tomorrow."
"I see, all right."
"Yeah."

After that spectacle…
Ogiso's father came upstairs to her room, and politely apologized to us.
Despite my own apologies, the explanation that I was the one who forcibly invited Ogiso, as well as the fact that she quit her job because of me, he simply took it all as "his daughter's problem."
He just said that the family had something to discuss today, and he apologetically sent us home, bowing his head.
"What was that…?"
"I'd like to know too…"
It seems that Touma also feels the same uneasiness that I do.
An entire family council to discuss whether she should perform at the school festival…
Even though he's such a strict father, he never said anything like, "Everyone be silent" or "I won't allow this."

"I'm… really not good with her."
Normally I'd force a comment right afterward, but I just can't do it now.
"Her family interfering that much… and she even thinks it's completely natural…"
Because… I feel like I've come across something incredibly remarkable.
To think that a family straight out of a soap opera still exists in reality, even now…
"Count me out… I can't imagine myself being in a situation like that."
"I… see…"
Which is why it had such a noticeable effect on Touma.
"I won't accept it… I'll lose if I do…"
"Touma…?"
Shivering as if she were cold, Touma looks up at the night sky overhead. A commonplace, and not too beautiful night sky.

"But you know… I had stuff like that happen at home too, years ago."
"I… see…"

"My curfew was at six, and whenever I was late, my mother would walk around restlessly in front of the house, and my father would lecture me really strictly."
Which is why I'm not sure whether she's listening to my silly story, or if she's shut me out completely. Perhaps it's something else entirely.
"When I secretly drank plum wine at my friend's place, I was busted the moment I came back home because my face was flushed red. He called my friend's home, and lectured me as well as my friend."
Even so, I continue my story, because I experienced that kind of drama at home in the past as well.
"Though they didn't care nearly as much about me once I entered middle school."
"They let you go?"
"…It's more the fact that my father left, really. Well, he pays plenty of child support, so I don't really have any right to complain."

"…I see you're still a half-assed idiot as usual, Kitahara."
"…I figured you were the only one who wouldn't be taken aback, Touma."
All three times I've talked about my family circumstances with my friendsーTakeya includedーtheir reactions were not very pleasant, so I've started avoiding talking about it with others.
"Well, I never knew my father's name or what he looked like. I haven't lived with my mother in years. The credit card she left me doesn't even have a limit."

"…You're as easy to understand as ever, Touma."
"…I thought you'd be somewhat taken aback, Kitahara."
"Well, I'm half-assed, as you say. I suppose that's why I can relate to both your family and Ogiso's family, Touma."
"And what would you understand… Well, I suppose you would."
"After all, if I were to look up your mother, I'd get over 100,000 results."
Her mother, a world-famous pianist.
All sorts of old gossip can be read from the top of the search results related to her as well as from her encyclopedia pages.
"My family circumstances aren't that complex. They're really perfectly normal. In some people's eyes, they're no big deal at all."

"But that's exactly why… it's fine for me to be frustrated, right? It's fine for me to be pointlessly angry at her, right?"
"Ogiso's a nice girl, isn't she…?"

"Even so…"
"She'll either become my worst enemy… or the greatest friend of my life."

"I promised Ogiso just before I left."
"Touma…?"

"I told her, 'If you can persuade your parents, I'll join the Light Music Club.'"
"Eh… Eh… Eehhh?"
This expression that she has kept hidden from me these past six months shines brighter than any gem in the night sky.
…Setting aside my earlier lackluster description of the night sky as "commonplace, and not too beautiful", that is.
"Why…? Eehhh!?"
"You don't want me to? Then I could take that back."
"But, but, but… I was already thinking of my next plan, too! I secretly swore to myself I'd definitely persuade you tomorrow!"

"You're bold, Kitahara. Did you plan to convince me with your tepid attitude…? You're getting ahead of yourself."
"Ah…"
…Did Setsuna incur something other than her anger?
